Create s1_library.js exporting a Library class: addBook(isbn, title, copies = 1) adds copies of a book (adding an isbn that already exists adds to its copies and keeps the first title) and throws an Error unless copies is a positive integer; copies(isbn) returns how many copies the library owns (0 for an unknown isbn); titles() returns the titles of all books sorted alphabetically. Include asserts that all pass, then run it with node.

Create s2_logs.py with parse_line(line) for access-log lines like 127.0.0.1 - - [10/Oct/2023:13:55:36 +0000] "GET /index.html HTTP/1.1" 200 2326 0.045 (ip, time, request, status, bytes, seconds). It returns a dict with ip, time (the text inside the brackets), method, path, status (int), bytes (int; "-" means 0) and seconds (float), and raises ValueError for a line that does not have that shape. Put the asserts under if __name__ == "__main__": and run it with python.

Create s3_matrix.js exporting a Matrix class: new Matrix(rows) takes an array of equal-length arrays of numbers and throws an Error for no rows, empty rows, rows of different lengths or anything that is not a finite number; shape() returns [rows, cols]; get(r, c) returns an entry and throws an Error outside the matrix; toArray() returns a copy of the rows. Include asserts that all pass, then run it with node.

Create s4_markdown.py with to_html(text): blocks separated by blank lines become

...

paragraphs (the lines inside a block are joined with one space, and the blocks are joined with "\n"), and the characters &, < and > are escaped as &, < and >. Put the asserts under if __name__ == "__main__": and run it with python.

Create s5_expr.js exporting evaluate(expr) that computes + - * / on numbers (integers and decimals) with the usual precedence and left-to-right order, allowing spaces; it throws an Error for division by zero and for anything it cannot parse. Include asserts that all pass, then run it with node.

Create s6_graph.py with a Graph class for a directed graph: add_node(n) (adding an existing node is not an error), add_edge(a, b, weight=1) which adds both nodes and raises ValueError unless weight is a positive number (adding an edge that exists replaces its weight), nodes() returning every node sorted, and neighbors(a) returning a sorted list of (b, weight) tuples. Put the asserts under if __name__ == "__main__": and run it with python.

Create s7_cache.js exporting a Cache class: new Cache(capacity) (it throws an Error unless capacity is a positive integer), set(key, value), get(key) (undefined when missing), has(key) and size(). When the cache is full, setting a new key evicts the least recently used entry, where both get and set count as a use. Include asserts that all pass, then run it with node.

Create s8_grades.py with a Gradebook class: add_student(name) (ValueError if it exists), add_assignment(name, max_points) (ValueError for a duplicate name or a max_points that is not a positive number), record(student, assignment, points) (KeyError for an unknown student or assignment, ValueError unless 0 <= points <= max_points; recording again replaces the score) and score(student, assignment) returning the points or None. Put the asserts under if __name__ == "__main__": and run it with python.

Create s9_board.html with three columns - elements with the ids "s9-todo", "s9-doing" and "s9-done", each holding a <ul> - plus an input with id "s9-new" and a button with id "s9-add". Clicking the button adds the input's text as an <li class="s9-card"> at the end of the To Do list and clears the input; blank text adds nothing. Put the logic in s9_board.js, loaded at the end of the body.

Create s10_desk.js that uses the EXISTING s1_library.js and s7_cache.js (require them; read them first so you use their real exports) and exports shelfLine(library): the library's titles() joined with ', ', or '(empty)' when it has no books. Include asserts that all pass, then run it with node.

Add checkout(isbn, member) and available(isbn) to the EXISTING Library in s1_library.js: checkout lends one copy to member, and available(isbn) is the copies minus the copies on loan. checkout throws an Error for an unknown isbn, when no copy is available, or when that member already has that book, and on a throw nothing changes. Run it with node.

Add parse_log(text) and bad_lines(text) to the EXISTING s2_logs.py: parse_log returns the parsed dicts of every valid line, skipping blank and malformed lines; bad_lines returns the 1-based line numbers of the malformed lines that are not blank. Run it with python.

Add add(other) and sub(other) to the EXISTING Matrix in s3_matrix.js, each returning a new Matrix and throwing an Error when the shapes differ; neither changes the matrices it is given. Run it with node.

Add headings to to_html in the EXISTING s4_markdown.py: a line that starts with 1 to 3 # characters and a space becomes <h1>, <h2> or <h3> with the rest of the line as its text, and it is always a block of its own, even with no blank line around it. Run it with python.
Make evaluate() in the EXISTING s5_expr.js handle parentheses and unary minus: '-(2+3)*2' is -10 and '2*-3' is -6. Run it with node.

Add bfs(start) to the EXISTING Graph in s6_graph.py returning the nodes reachable from start in breadth-first order, visiting neighbors in sorted order; an unknown start raises KeyError. Run it with python.
Add delete(key) and clear() to the EXISTING Cache in s7_cache.js: delete returns true when it removed an entry and false otherwise. Run it with node.

Add percent(student) to the EXISTING Gradebook in s8_grades.py returning the student's total points divided by the total max_points of the assignments they have a score for, as a percentage rounded to 2 decimals, or None when they have no scores; an unknown student raises KeyError. Run it with python.

Give every card in the EXISTING s9 board (s9_board.html, s9_board.js) a button with the class "s9-right" and one with the class "s9-left" that move the card to the end of the next or the previous column (To Do, Doing, Done); moving right from Done or left from To Do does nothing.
Add availability(library, isbn) to the EXISTING s10_desk.js and export it: it returns 'available/copies' for that book, e.g. '1/2'. Run it with node.
